title: Code-owner resolution only yields project members with a linked GitHub login, and fails soft
answers: Why isn't a CODEOWNERS team or email suggested as a reviewer?
How are CODEOWNERS handles resolved to reviewers in signals?
What happens when CODEOWNERS is missing or GitHub calls fail?
body:
In ownership_reviewers.py:suggest_repository_owners, every owner handle (user, @org/team, email) is reduced to GitHub logins, then filtered via resolve_org_github_login_to_users and team.all_users_with_access(). Non-members and members without a linked GitHub identity are dropped; emails match case-insensitively via Lower(email) plus get_github_login().
Team handles are expanded with github.list_team_members and only for the repository's own org; slugs must match _TEAM_SLUG.
CODEOWNERS is read from the first of .github/CODEOWNERS, CODEOWNERS, docs/CODEOWNERS (_CODEOWNERS_LOCATIONS); last matching rule wins; files >=3 MB, negations and section patterns are skipped; paths capped at _MAX_PATHS and '..' rejected.
All failures log and return [] so existing author-based suggestions stay intact. Keep new lookups inside those try/except blocks. The scout prompt (scout_harness/prompt.py) states the same rules and should be updated in tandem.
